name: GLB benchmark 1: score Three.js answers by the GLB they export
description: Phase 1 tooling for docs/13-glb-code-track.md: a GLB parser, a GLB mode for the scene validator that clicks Export and checks the downloaded file, a configurable system prompt and sampling for teacher_generate, a resumable benchmark runner over bench/glb/models.json, a report with confidence intervals and head-to-head counts, and a blind contact sheet for human rating. The owner then runs untuned Muse Glimmer and ccore's Qwen3.5-4B-GLB-3D-Coder on the 48 briefs in bench/glb/briefs.jsonl and decides on phase 2 with the rules in docs/13 section 7.

userStories.title: glb_check.mjs: parse a GLB and count meshes, triangles, animations and bounds
userStories.description: As the evaluator, I want a dependency-free GLB parser so that every exported asset can be checked and measured. Use the exact file and function names given in the steps: other names fail review.
steps: Create tests/js/glb_util.mjs exporting `makeGlb({triangles = 1, indexed = true, animations = 0, meshes = 1, version = 2, badMagic = false, truncate = false})` that writes a minimal valid GLB Buffer by hand (12-byte header, JSON chunk padded with spaces to 4 bytes, BIN chunk padded with zeros): one node per mesh, one primitive per mesh, a FLOAT VEC3 POSITION accessor with min and max, an optional UNSIGNED_SHORT index accessor, and `animations` dummy animation entries with valid sampler and channel objects. The flags produce the broken variants used in tests.

Create scripts/glb_check.mjs exporting `parseGlb(buf)` per docs/13 section 5.2: returns {ok, reason, bytes, version, meshes, primitives, triangles, vertices, materials, nodes, animations, bbox:{min, max, size}}. Triangle rules: mode 4 or absent counts indices.count/3 (POSITION.count/3 when not indexed), modes 5 and 6 count count-2, modes 0-3 count 0. bbox is the union of POSITION min/max with node transforms ignored. reason is 'bad_glb' for wrong magic, version other than 2, declared length different from the buffer, missing or unparsable JSON chunk; 'empty_glb' for zero meshes or zero triangles; null when ok. It must never throw.
Add a CLI to the same file: `node scripts/glb_check.mjs FILE.glb` prints the result as one JSON line and exits 0 when ok, 1 otherwise. Guard the CLI so importing the module does not run it.

Create tests/js/glb_check.test.mjs and import it from tests/js/index.js. Cover: one indexed triangle, 12 non-indexed triangles, 3 meshes, 2 animations, bbox values equal the accessor min/max, wrong magic, version 1, truncated buffer, zero triangles, random bytes, and the CLI exit codes on a temp file.
acceptanceCriteria: Files are named exactly scripts/glb_check.mjs, tests/js/glb_util.mjs and tests/js/glb_check.test.mjs, and tests/js/index.js imports the new test file
parseGlb returns reason 'bad_glb' for wrong magic, version 1, truncation and random bytes, and 'empty_glb' for zero triangles, without throwing (each asserted)
Triangle counts are asserted for indexed and non-indexed input, and animations and bbox are asserted against the values makeGlb wrote
Importing scripts/glb_check.mjs prints nothing and does not exit the process (asserted)
glb_check.mjs imports only node: built-ins (asserted by reading its import lines in the test)
`bash scripts/check.sh` passes (syntax checks, pytest, node tests; offline)
Any script flag or behaviour you changed or added is described in README.md or the doc the story names

userStories.title: validate_scenes.mjs --mode glb: allow GLTFExporter, click Export, check the downloaded GLB
userStories.description: As the evaluator, I want the existing validator to score asset pages by the GLB they export, so that every model is judged on the same file a game engine would import, while the scene mode stays exactly as it is. Use the exact file and function names given in the steps: other names fail review.
steps: Add flags `--mode scene|glb` (default scene) and `--glb-dir DIR` (default data/glb, used only in glb mode) to scripts/validate_scenes.mjs. Keep every scene-mode code path and result unchanged.

In glb mode: (a) static checks allow Three.js core and examples/jsm/exporters/GLTFExporter.js from cdnjs.cloudflare.com, cdn.jsdelivr.net or unpkg.com, directly or via an import map, at any version; any other addon is 'bad_import' and any other host 'external_dep'. (b) Route every allowed core URL to node_modules/three/build/three.module.js and every GLTFExporter URL to node_modules/three/examples/jsm/exporters/GLTFExporter.js; when the requested version is not 0.160.0 record stats.three_requested and stats.version_rewritten = true (not a failure). (c) 'static' and 'no_loop' are not reasons. (d) After the screenshot, click the first button, a or [role=button] element whose visible text matches /export|download|glb/i, wait up to 20 s for a Playwright download, save it to <glb-dir>/<id>.glb and record stats.export_ms. Reasons: 'no_export_button', 'no_download', 'export_error' (a page error raised after the click). (e) Run parseGlb from scripts/glb_check.mjs on the file and store its result in stats.glb; add its reason ('bad_glb' or 'empty_glb') when not ok.

Create fixtures in tests/fixtures/glb_raw/, each a raw answer JSON like tests/fixtures/raw/b000.json whose content is an html code block: g_ok (import map to jsDelivr three@0.160.0 plus three/addons/, a cube in a Group named asset, an Export GLB button using GLTFExporter binary:true and an anchor download), g_unpkg (same but unpkg three@0.165.0, expected ok with version_rewritten), g_anim (exports one AnimationClip, expected stats.glb.animations = 1), g_nobutton, g_throws (button handler throws), g_orbit (imports OrbitControls), g_trunc (finish_reason length).

Create tests/js/validate_glb.test.mjs (imported from tests/js/index.js) that runs the validator in glb mode on a temp copy of the fixtures with temp scenes, shots, glb and report paths, and asserts each fixture's ok and reasons; it also runs scene mode on tests/fixtures/raw and asserts the report equals what scene mode produced before this story (capture the expected rows once into tests/fixtures/glb_raw/scene_mode_expected.jsonl, compare id, ok and reasons only).
acceptanceCriteria: g_ok, g_unpkg and g_anim pass in glb mode with a .glb file written to the temp glb dir; g_unpkg has stats.version_rewritten true and g_anim has stats.glb.animations equal to 1 (asserted)

Scene mode on tests/fixtures/raw gives the same id, ok and reasons as scene_mode_expected.jsonl (asserted)

userStories.title: glb_bench.py and models.json: one resumable command per model, generate then validate
userStories.description: As the owner, I want one command that runs every enabled model on the 48 briefs and validates the answers, refuses unsafe runs, and shows the exact commands first. Use the exact file and function names given in the steps: other names fail review.
steps: Create bench/glb/models.json with the six rows of docs/13 section 4.3 (fields: name, provider 'ollama' or 'baseten', model, system (a path under prompts/), temperature, top_p, top_k, min_p, think, enabled, paid). ccore-q8 and glimmer are enabled; the rest are not; spark-open has paid true.

Create scripts/glb_bench.py with argparse: `--out-root DIR` (required), `--models bench/glb/models.json`, `--briefs bench/glb/briefs.jsonl`, `--only NAME` (repeatable; selects rows even if disabled), `--limit N`, `--num-ctx 49152`, `--max-tokens 40000`, `--allow-paid`, `--dry-run`. Pure function `plan(models, args) -> list[list[str]]` builds, per model, the teacher_generate command (--ollama-native for ollama rows, --system, sampling flags only when set, --think when true, --concurrency 1, --out <root>/<name>/raw) and the validator command (node scripts/validate_scenes.mjs --mode glb with --raw, --scenes, --shots, --glb-dir, --report <root>/<name>/validation.jsonl under <root>/<name>/).

Refusals (non-zero exit, clear message, nothing run): --out-root inside data/ or out/; a selected row whose system file is missing or still contains 'PASTE_CCORE_SYSTEM_PROMPT_HERE'; a paid row without --allow-paid; an unknown --only name. In a real run (not --dry-run) check `ollama list` once and stop with the pull command if a selected ollama model is absent. Each command is printed before it runs; --dry-run prints them all and runs nothing.

Create tests/py/test_glb_bench.py: plan() output for the two enabled rows (flags and order), --only selecting a disabled row, every refusal above, placeholder detection on a tmp copy of prompts/ccore_glb_system.txt, and a --dry-run subprocess run that creates no files under the tmp out root. No test calls ollama or node.
acceptanceCriteria: Files are named exactly bench/glb/models.json, scripts/glb_bench.py and tests/py/test_glb_bench.py, and models.json has the six rows with only ccore-q8 and glimmer enabled
plan() emits generate then validate per model with the per-model sampling from models.json (asserted for ccore-q8: temperature 0.8, top-k 40, top-p 0.95, min-p 0, --think)

userStories.title: glb_report.py: pass rate with intervals, failures, cost, domains and head to head
userStories.description: As the owner, I want one report that compares the models on the metrics in docs/13 section 5.3, with honest uncertainty, so the phase 2 decision rests on numbers. Use the exact file and function names given in the steps: other names fail review.
steps: Create tests/fixtures/glb_bench/ with two model folders (m_a, m_b), each with validation.jsonl rows for 6 briefs and raw/<id>.json rows with usage {completion_tokens, seconds}, plus a briefs.jsonl of those 6 briefs (mixing static, animated and set kinds) and a ratings fixture rating.csv with key_map.json in the format glb_sheet.mjs will write (key, brief, rating; key -> {model, id}).

Create scripts/glb_report.py with pure functions: `wilson(k, n, z=1.96)`, `load_model(dir)`, `metrics(rows, raws, briefs)` returning the section 5.3 metrics (pass rate, export rate, animated pass requiring stats.glb.animations > 0, median and max triangles of passes, share of passes at or under 5,000 triangles, reason counts, median completion tokens, median seconds, total seconds, pass by domain), `head_to_head(a, b)` returning both/only_a/only_b/neither counts, and `recognisable(ratings, key_map, ids)` where a missing or failed item counts as 0 and the rate is the share rated 1 or 2 over all briefs.

CLI: `--root DIR --briefs FILE [--ratings rating.csv [--key-map key_map.json]]` (key-map defaults to the file beside rating.csv). Every subfolder of root with a validation.jsonl is a model. Writes <root>/report.json and <root>/report.md (one table row per model with pass rate and its 95% interval, then failures, by domain and head-to-head tables). Briefs absent from a model's validation count as failures with reason 'missing'.

Create tests/py/test_glb_report.py: wilson values against known numbers (k=0, k=n, k=24 of 48), each metric on the fixtures, head-to-head counts, the missing-brief rule, recognisable with and without a rating for every item, and that the markdown names both models and contains the interval.
acceptanceCriteria: Files are named exactly scripts/glb_report.py, tests/py/test_glb_report.py and tests/fixtures/glb_bench/
wilson(24, 48) is asserted to round to (0.364, 0.636) at 3 decimals, and wilson(0, 48) has a lower bound of 0
Animated pass counts an animated brief only when it passes and stats.glb.animations > 0 (asserted with one fixture that passes with 0 animations)
A brief missing from a model's validation.jsonl counts as a failure with reason 'missing' (asserted)
The report contains only numbers computed from the input files; with no --ratings the recognisable column says 'not rated'

userStories.title: glb_sheet.mjs: render exported GLBs to contact sheets and a blind rating file
userStories.description: As the owner, I want to look at every exported asset next to its brief without knowing which model made it, because the mesh track showed that valid is not the same as right. Use the exact file and function names given in the steps: other names fail review.
steps: Create scripts/glb_sheet.mjs: `--root DIR --out DIR [--briefs bench/glb/briefs.jsonl] [--size 256] [--seed 1]`. For every <root>/<model>/glb/<id>.glb, load it in headless Chromium with the local node_modules/three 0.160.0 and examples/jsm/loaders/GLTFLoader.js (route the URLs locally as validate_scenes.mjs does, no network), frame its bounding box, and render a 3/4 view and a top view on a light grey background with one hemisphere and one directional light. Write <out>/<model>/<id>.png (both views side by side) and <out>/<model>/sheet.png (a grid with the id under each tile).

Write <out>/rating.csv with columns key, brief, image, rating (rating empty) in an order shuffled by a seeded PRNG, one row per model x brief (briefs with no GLB still get a row whose image is empty, so the rater sees the miss), with keys like r001 that do not reveal the model, and <out>/key_map.json mapping key -> {model, id}. Briefs come from --briefs.
A GLB that fails to load is listed in <out>/skipped.json and does not stop the run. A rerun skips PNGs that already exist.

Create tests/js/glb_sheet.test.mjs (imported from tests/js/index.js): build two tiny GLBs with tests/js/glb_util.mjs plus one corrupt file under a temp root for two models, run the script, and assert PNG files exist with the expected width, sheet.png exists per model, rating.csv has one row per model x brief with no model name in it, key_map.json maps every key, the corrupt file is in skipped.json, and the same seed gives the same order.
acceptanceCriteria: Files are named exactly scripts/glb_sheet.mjs and tests/js/glb_sheet.test.mjs, and tests/js/index.js imports the test
rating.csv contains no model name and key_map.json covers every row (asserted)
Briefs without a GLB appear in rating.csv with an empty image (asserted)
A corrupt GLB is listed in skipped.json and the other files still render (asserted)
No network request leaves the page (asserted by counting non-local requests)

metadata.standingRule: Offline-only PRD. Ralph builds and tests tools with tiny fixtures, fake generators and GLB files built inside the tests. It never calls Ollama, never pulls a model, never runs the benchmark and never writes under data/, out/ or eval/. The default (scene) mode of validate_scenes.mjs and the default behaviour of teacher_generate.py must not change: existing pilots were scored with them. Do not edit bench/glb/briefs.jsonl, prompts/system.txt, prompts/system_glb.txt or prompts/ccore_glb_system.txt.
guardrails: Work offline. Tests use fixtures under tests/fixtures and mocked HTTP. Never call Baseten, Meta, Hugging Face or any remote service from a story, a test or a script you run. The only network use allowed is `npm install` and `.venv/bin/pip install` of packages the story names.
Never commit, push, tag or publish. autoCommit is off and the owner commits.

Never delete, overwrite or reformat anything under data/, out/, eval/, .env or .venv. They are the owner's data (a long Glimmer generation run may be writing data/raw right now). Tests write only to temporary directories.

Do not start long jobs. Any command that would run more than about 5 minutes (corpus generation, training, GGUF conversion, evals) is written as a script plus docs and left for the owner. A live smoke call to the local Ollama is allowed only if the story says so, with at most 2 briefs, and must skip cleanly when Ollama is down. Never rent GPUs or run `runpodctl` with anything that creates a pod.
Edit only the files named in the story's steps, plus their tests and the doc the story names. Do not change prompts/system.txt: every existing raw answer was generated against it.

Match the surrounding code: short comments that explain why, argparse CLIs, resumable file-per-item outputs, no new dependency the story does not name. Python runs with `.venv/bin/python`; Node scripts are ESM `.mjs` (Node 22).
Three.js stays pinned at 0.160.0 and the validator keeps serving the local copy in place of the CDN URL.
Python scripts must stay importable without heavy deps: import torch, transformers, trl or peft only inside functions or under `if __name__ == '__main__'` so pytest can import them.
Record only real results. Never invent pass rates, token counts, timings or costs; where a number is unknown write 'not measured'.
Debug output goes to data/ or a temp dir, never into scripts/ or docs/.
If the spec is wrong or impossible, do the closest thing that works and explain the difference in `notes`. If you cannot finish a story, set `notes` to why and stop; do not mark it passing.
